doc.title: Jerry Coker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 18, 2023

title: Jazz-musician parents and record collection
summary: Coker's father and mother were jazz musicians with a huge record collection; they learned by ear, with no teachers then.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: A few. A few. Because before I started playing I was listening to the Hit Parade and that sort of thing so I was exposed to what was going on. But I also, I must tell you that my father was a jazz musician and so was my mother. And they had a huge record collection so that I had become so familiar with it from the time I was very young it was going on around me. So yeah there was an advantage.
Definitely. Did you start to be curious about what your mother and father were doing with this improvisation thing? Like how are they making up that music?
How were they making the music?

Well if you were watching them play, either at home or perhaps you saw them on a gig and they started playing their instruments and they weren’t reading the music, if they were making it up, did you wonder how that happened and were curious about it?
Were you curious how your parents were able to improvise?

By experience, playing with others, listening carefully to both, and good ears and a good memory for music. So yeah, they learned what they learned mostly from listening. There were no places to study. You know there were no teachers, that was a whole new thing.
What were — do you recall any of the songs they would have played back then? If they were jazz musicians were they playing Duke Ellington and the standards?
Yes. And perhaps like “Take the A Train,” that kind of music?

Yeah. Right. And my father played — continued to play a long time after his youth. So it was close to it and so when my brother and I grew up and we started playing our records, he got interested in what records we were listening to, and he kept up with us very well and so did my mother. They came to hear us play when they could.
